response: Yes, primary angioplasty (also known as percutaneous coronary intervention or PCI) is an acceptable alternative to thrombolysis for treating acute myocardial infarction (heart attack). In fact, primary angioplasty is often considered the preferred treatment option when it can be performed promptly by an experienced team. It has been shown to have higher success rates and lower complication rates compared to thrombolysis, especially when done within 90 minutes of first medical contact.
